about: How a consumer that needs 'the' yield series of a crop in a country picks one (E156). A series is never spliced from two sources: for each crop and country the consumer uses ONE source — the first in national_precedence that holds a national series for it. A consumer may also name a source explicitly. This order is the platform's stated choice, changed only here (a reviewed commit).

why.FAOSTAT QCL bulk: the longest series (1961→), one definition for every country, calendar years
why.EUROSTAT apro_cpsh1: used where FAOSTAT holds no series for the crop (durum wheat), EU-27 / EFTA / UK / candidates

never_in_history.USDA FAS PSD: market years and some definitions differ from FAO's (milled rice, oils, shelled almonds) — read only as the latest-season estimate, never spliced into a history

named_only.USDA NASS Quick Stats: the US national series and one per state from the primary US publisher (FAOSTAT's US figures come from NASS) — read when a consumer names it (a state's series, or NASS's own US figure); not in the precedence, so a US national history keeps the one definition every other country has
named_only.EUROSTAT apro_cpshr: one series per NUTS-2 region (regional only — the national series is apro_cpsh1's), read when a consumer names the source and region
named_only.STATCAN 32-10-0359-01: Canada and one series per province from the national statistics office — read when a consumer names it (a province's series, or StatCan's own Canada figure, e.g. durum wheat, which FAOSTAT does not separate)

regional: a regional series (region_code ≠ '') is read only when a consumer names its source and region
every_reviewed_source: each reviewed yield source (services.reference.yield_sources) is in exactly one of national_precedence, never_in_history or named_only — a new source states its role here before it lands (tests/integration/test_yield_series.py)
